title: Chipa (Paraguayan cassava and cheese bread rolls)

ingredients.name: firm fresh cheese such as queso fresco or low-moisture mozzarella, grated (stands in for queso Paraguay)

steps: Heat the oven to 200 C and line a baking tray with parchment.
Rub the butter into the cassava starch, cornmeal and salt with your fingertips until the mixture looks like damp sand.
Work in the grated cheese, anise seeds, eggs and enough milk to make a smooth, pliable dough that does not stick to your hands.
Knead briefly for 2 minutes, then rest the dough for 10 minutes.
Shape the dough into small rolls, rings or horseshoes about 6 cm long and place them on the tray.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and golden. Eat warm with mate cocido, coffee or as a snack.

title: Chipa guasu (Paraguayan fresh corn and cheese cake)

ingredients.name: fresh or frozen sweet corn kernels
fresh white cheese, crumbled or grated (queso fresco or mozzarella)

steps: Heat the oven to 190 C and grease a 22 cm baking dish.
Cook the onion in the butter for 5 to 6 minutes until soft and translucent but not coloured.
Blend or pulse half the corn with the milk into a rough, thick puree.
Mix the puree with the remaining whole kernels, cooked onion, cheese, eggs and salt.
Pour the batter into the dish and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden on top and set in the centre.
Let it rest for 10 minutes, then cut into squares and serve warm, often alongside grilled meat.

title: Chipa so'o (Paraguayan beef-filled cassava bread)
steps: Cook the onion, pepper and garlic in a little oil for 5 minutes, add the beef with salt, pepper and oregano and fry until well browned and fairly dry. Cool, then fold in the chopped egg.
Heat the oven to 200 C and line a tray with parchment.
Rub the butter into the starch, cornmeal and 1 tsp salt, then work in the cheese, eggs and milk to make a soft dough.

Take a piece of dough about the size of a small egg, flatten it into a disc in your palm, place a spoonful of meat filling in the centre and fold the dough around it, sealing well into a ball or oval.
Place the filled chipas on the tray and bake for about 25 minutes until golden.
Let them cool for 10 minutes, then serve warm as a snack or with an asado.

title: Kaguyjy (Paraguayan hominy pudding, mazamorra)

ingredients.name: dried hominy (peeled white corn), or 2 cans (about 800 g) cooked hominy

steps: If using dried hominy, soak it in cold water overnight, then drain.

Cook the soaked hominy in the 1.5 litres of fresh water over low heat for about 2 hours until the kernels are very tender and have split open, adding hot water if needed. If using canned hominy, drain and just warm it with a little water for 10 minutes.
Add the milk, sugar and cinnamon stick and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pudding is soft, creamy and lightly thickened.
Remove the cinnamon stick and stir in the vanilla if using.
Serve warm or cooled in bowls. For variations, sweeten with honey instead of sugar, or leave out the milk and just add sugar to the cooked corn.

title: Kamby arro (Paraguayan cold rice pudding)
steps: Rinse the rice well under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, and drain.
Put the rice, water, milk, sugar, lemon peel and cinnamon stick in a heavy pot and bring to a gentle boil, stirring.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 40 to 50 minutes, stirring often so the rice does not stick, until it is creamy and thick.
Remove the lemon peel and cinnamon stick and spoon the pudding into bowls or a dish.
Cool, then chill for at least 2 hours, and sprinkle with ground cinnamon before serving cold.

title: Kiveve (Paraguayan sweet pumpkin and cornmeal pudding)

ingredients.name: orange-fleshed pumpkin or butternut squash, peeled and cubed
fresh white cheese, finely chopped (queso fresco)

steps: Boil the pumpkin in just enough water to cover for 15 to 20 minutes until it is very soft.
Mash the pumpkin in its cooking water to a thick puree.
Stir in the sugar and salt, then bring back to a gentle simmer over low heat.
Rain the cornmeal in slowly while stirring constantly, then cook for about 10 minutes until the mixture thickens and the cornmeal is cooked through.
Stir in the chopped cheese and take the pot off the heat.
Serve warm or cold in bowls, with milk poured over each portion to taste.

title: Kosereva (Paraguayan sour orange peel preserve)

ingredients.name: sour oranges (Seville), or grapefruit rinds as a substitute

steps: Cut the oranges in halves, squeeze out the juice for another use and scoop out the pulp, leaving only the thick peel.
Put the peels in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil, simmer for 10 minutes, then drain. Repeat twice more with fresh water to remove most of the bitterness.
Combine the sugar, molasses and 500 ml water in a wide heavy pot and heat until the sugar dissolves.
Add the blanched peels, bring to a simmer and cook gently for 1.5 to 2 hours, turning occasionally, until the peels are translucent and dark and the syrup is thick.
Cool in the syrup and store in a clean jar in the fridge. Serve a piece of peel with a spoon of syrup, often with fresh cheese.

title: Lampreado (Paraguayan fried cassava and beef cakes)

ingredients.name: cassava (manioc), peeled and cut in chunks

steps: Boil the cassava in salted water for 25 to 30 minutes until soft, then drain and remove any woody centre fibres.
Mash the cassava thoroughly while hot until smooth.
Fry the onion and garlic in a little oil for 5 minutes, add the beef with salt and pepper and cook until browned and dry.
Mix the beef mixture and the breadcrumbs into the mashed cassava until you have a firm, mouldable dough.
Shape into flat patties about 8 cm wide and 1.5 cm thick.
Shallow-fry the patties in hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp, and drain on paper towels. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Mbeju (Paraguayan cassava starch and cheese flatbread)

ingredients.name: fresh white cheese, shredded (queso fresco or mozzarella)

steps: Rub the fat into the starch and salt until crumbly, then add the cheese.
Sprinkle in the warm milk a little at a time and work the mixture with your hands until it holds together when squeezed but is still slightly crumbly.
Heat a heavy non-stick or cast iron skillet over medium heat.
Press a layer of the mixture about 1 cm thick into the skillet in a round, pressing it together firmly. The cheese will melt and bind it.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the underside is golden and crisp, then flip and cook the other side for the same time.
Serve warm, cut in wedges, with coffee or mate cocido.

title: Piracaldo (Paraguayan fish soup)

ingredients.name: river or catfish fillets, in chunks (or any firm white fish)
fresh hot chile, chopped, to taste

steps: Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion, pepper and garlic for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until they collapse into a sauce.
Pour in the water, season with salt and pepper and bring to a boil.
Add the fish and simmer very gently for 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish is cooked and starts to flake into the broth.
Stir in the parsley and the chopped chile, taste for seasoning and simmer for 2 minutes more.
Serve hot in bowls with bread or boiled cassava.

title: Sopa paraguaya (Paraguayan cornbread with cheese and onion)

ingredients.name: fresh white cheese, crumbled (queso fresco or mozzarella)

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and grease a 24 cm square baking dish.
Cook the onions in half the butter for 10 minutes over low heat until very soft and golden, then let them cool slightly.
Beat the remaining butter with the egg yolks until fluffy, then stir in the milk, cornmeal, salt, cheese and cooked onions.
Whisk the egg whites to firm peaks and fold them gently into the batter to keep it light.
Pour into the dish and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until risen and golden on top, with a skewer coming out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes and cut into squares. Serve warm.

title: Soyo (Paraguayan minced beef soup)

ingredients.name: lean beef, very finely minced (pounded to a paste in a mortar if you can)

steps: Pound or process the beef until it is a fine, almost paste-like mince and season it with salt, pepper and oregano.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion, pepper and garlic for 5 minutes, then add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the meat and cook, breaking it apart, for 5 minutes until it changes colour.
Pour in the water or stock, add the potatoes and carrot and bring to a boil.
Simmer, partly covered, for 25 to 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the soup is thick and flavourful.
Adjust the seasoning and serve hot.

title: Tereré (Paraguayan iced yerba mate with herbs)

ingredients.name: fresh mint or lemon balm leaves

steps: Fill about two-thirds of a mate cup or large glass with yerba mate.
Cover the top with your palm, turn it upside down and shake gently so the fine dust gathers near the top, then tilt back upright with the leaves banked on one side.
Insert a bombilla (metal filter straw) into the empty side and press it against the bottom.
Add a few ice cubes and pour a little ice-cold water down the bombilla side to moisten the leaves, then wait a few seconds.
Add the bruised mint or lemon balm and the citrus slices to the cup or the water jug, and refill with ice-cold water each time it is sipped dry.
Pass the cup around a circle, refilling with cold water as it is drunk, until the flavour fades.

title: Vori vori (Paraguayan chicken soup with cornmeal and cheese dumplings)
steps: Soften the onion, pepper and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the tomatoes and oregano and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and the water, season with salt, bring to a boil and simmer for 35 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the broth has taken on flavour.
Remove the chicken, shred the meat off the bones and return it to the pot, keeping 150 ml of hot broth aside.
Mix the cornmeal, cheese and a pinch of salt in a bowl, then add enough of the hot reserved broth to make a dough that is moist but holds together.
Roll the dough into small balls about the size of a grape and drop them into the simmering soup.
Cook the dumplings for about 5 minutes until they float and are cooked through. Add a little hot water if the soup is too thick, adjust the seasoning and serve.
